items.q: Obstructive sleep apnoea differs from central sleep apnoea on polysomnography by what?
o: Continued respiratory effort against a collapsed airway versus absent effort
items.exp: Obstructive events show thoracic and abdominal effort without airflow (paradoxical motion), while central events pause effort itself from drive failure; mixed patterns transition between the two.
r: Correct. Effort present obstructed, absent central.
items.kp: Pushing with no air: obstruction. No push at all: central.

items.q: Apnoea hypopnoea index severity bands are which?
o: Under 5 normal; 5 to 15 mild; 15 to 30 moderate; over 30 severe
items.exp: AHI counts apnoeas plus hypopnoeas per sleep hour; bands guide CPAP versus conservative decisions alongside symptoms and desaturation burden. Night to night variability and positional disease nuance single numbers.
r: Incorrect. AHI is the defining metric.
items.kp: Five mild, fifteen moderate, thirty severe.

items.q: First line therapy for moderate to severe adult OSA is what?
o: CPAP with adherence support (mask fit, humidification, titration)
items.exp: CPAP pneumatically stents collapse across levels and reverses sleepiness and cardiovascular strain when worn; surgery follows mapping or intolerance, tracheostomy only for refractory life threat.
r: Incorrect. One operation never fits all levels.
Incorrect. Infection is not the disease.
items.kp: Pressure mask first for grown up apnoea.

items.q: Strongest single examination predictor cluster for adult OSA includes which?
o: Obesity with large neck circumference plus retrognathia and tonsillar hypertrophy
items.exp: Fat loaded pharyngeal walls, small bony enclosure and bulky lymphoid tissue narrow the collapsible segment; STOP Bang scores bundle snoring, tiredness, observed pauses, pressure, BMI, age, neck and gender.
r: Correct. Fat neck, small jaw, big tonsils.
items.kp: Fat neck, pushed back jaw: collapsing throat.

items.q: Cardiovascular consequence most tightly tied to untreated severe OSA is which?
o: Resistant hypertension with atrial fibrillation and stroke risk
items.exp: Nightly hypoxia and arousal surges reset sympathetic and endothelial tone; CPAP lowers pressure and fibrillation burden in adherent users. Driving and occupational risk parallel cardiac harm.
r: Correct. Pressure, rhythm and brain events.
Incorrect. Dissection links connective tissue and pressure spikes differently.
items.kp: Apnoea nights grow pressure and clots.

items.q: First line treatment for childhood OSA with adenotonsillar hypertrophy is what?
items.exp: Bulky lymphoid tissue dominates paediatric obstruction and removal cures most; obesity, Down syndrome and craniofacial syndromes need sleep studies and tailored multilevel care.
r: Incorrect. Children rarely tolerate lifelong masks first.
Incorrect. Steroids shrink modestly, not gross hypertrophy.
Incorrect. Bypass is rescue, not first line.

items.q: Drug induced sleep endoscopy contributes to OSA care chiefly by what?
o: Mapping collapse levels and patterns (palate, tongue base, epiglottis) to direct surgery or stimulation
items.exp: Sedated endoscopy watches where the airway shuts (concentric palate, anteroposterior tongue, floppy epiglottis), so operations address the right level instead of ritual UPPP. Diagnosis still rests on sleep studies.
r: Correct. Collapse map guides knife or device.
items.kp: Watch it collapse asleep, then aim surgery.

items.q: Mandibular advancement devices help OSA by which mechanism and suit whom?
o: Jaw and tongue protrusion enlarging retrolingual airway; mild to moderate disease or CPAP intolerance
items.exp: Protrusion tensions genioglossus and opens tongue base collapse during sleep; dentition, jaw joints and severity bound candidacy, with follow up studies confirming control.
r: Correct. Forward jaw, mild disease or intolerance.
Incorrect. Weight loss helps, not gain.
items.kp: Push jaw forward, open throat behind tongue.

items.q: Why do opioids and sedatives endanger undiagnosed OSA patients perioperatively?
o: Blunted arousal and pharyngeal tone convert partial obstruction to complete, with supine REM rebound after surgery
items.exp: Arousal rescues apnoeics nightly; drugs remove the rescue while relaxing dilators, so monitored beds, multimodal analgesia and CPAP resumption plans precede elective lists.
r: Correct. No arousal, no tone, closed throat.
Incorrect. Drying is trivial beside obstruction.
items.kp: Sleepy drugs silence the wake up rescue.

items.q: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation treats OSA by what action and fits which patients?
o: Stimulates tongue protrusion timed to breathing in CPAP failures without complete concentric palatal collapse
items.exp: Implanted cuffs drive genioglossus with respiration, rescuing tongue base collapse; DISE excludes complete concentric palatal shutdown and BMI bounds candidacy in trials.
r: Correct. Tongue pacing for mapped failures.
items.kp: Pace the tongue forward each breath.
